_meta.note: Generic OBD-II codes (SAE J2012). Meanings follow the standard; causes and likelihoods are drafted by AI from general automotive knowledge, 2026-11-16, and need a mechanic's review. Manufacturer-specific codes are not listed.

Worn wheel bearing / damaged reluctor ring

codes.title: System too lean (bank 1)

causes.text: Vacuum or intake air leak (cracked hose, intake gasket)

causes.text: Dirty or faulty mass air flow (MAF) sensor
causes.diy_check: Check the air filter and the MAF connector

codes.title: Engine overheating

causes.diy_check: When the engine is COLD, check the coolant level. Never open a hot radiator cap
With the engine hot and idling, the radiator fan should switch on

codes.notes: Stop as soon as it is safe and switch the engine off. Driving while overheating can destroy the engine.

codes.title: Turbo overboost

causes.text: Stuck wastegate or boost control valve
Vacuum hose to the wastegate split
causes.diy_check: Check small vacuum hoses around the turbo

codes.notes: Drive gently; avoid hard acceleration.

causes.text: Dirty or faulty boost pressure sensor

codes.title: Turbo underboost

causes.text: Boost leak (split intercooler hose, loose clamp)

codes.notes: Often causes limp mode (low power). Common on diesels.
